production.note: US model years, 2016 onward. Mazda's March 2015 release introduces the fourth-generation car as the 2016 MX-5 Miata. Still on sale: Mazda USA's vehicle page is titled '2026 Mazda MX-5 Miata Convertible Roadster' (mazda-usa-mx5-page).

body.note: Soft top ('Black cloth convertible top'). The retractable-hardtop MX-5 Miata RF is sold under its own name and is a separate record.

aspiration.note: No forced induction is listed on Mazda's sheet; the words 'naturally aspirated' do not appear on it.

transmission.note: 'SKYACTIV-MT 6-speed manual transmission' standard; '6-speed Sport automatic' optional.

powerHp.note: Quote: "181 hp @ 7000 rpm" (Horsepower row, same for Sport, Club and Grand Touring). The launch rating was 155 hp: "Powering all North American models will be a 2.0-liter SKYACTIV engine, rated at 155 horsepower and 148 lb-ft of torque." (mazda-2016-mx5-club-release). It rose for 2019: "181 horsepower at 7,000 rpm—a 17-percent improvement" (mazda-2019-mx5-release) and is still 181 hp on Mazda USA's 2026 page (mazda-usa-mx5-page), so the reference year uses the longer-lived 181 hp rating.

weightLb.note: 2019 soft top with the six-speed manual. Quote: "2,339 (MT) / 2,388 (AT)" (Curb weight (lbs) row). The 2016 car was 2,332 lb manual and 2,381 lb automatic (mazda-2016-mx5-club-release); Mazda says 'the 2019 MX-5 gains just 7 lbs. from previous models' (mazda-2019-mx5-release).
